source.version_note: Published International Journal of Social Robotics 15(5):867–877, online 26 March 2023 and issue May 2023. Accepted 3 March 2023. Supplied article includes all main results, declarations, 46 references and author biographies.
source.verification_method: All eleven supplied pages read, including three figures and four tables visually checked in page renders. Publisher and Crossref verify title, four authors and dates. Selected cited-source identities checked using Crossref, MIT Press and DBLP; those checks are not full cited-paper/book readings.

citation.title: Mind Perception in HRI: Exploring Users’ Attribution of Mental and Emotional States to Robots with Different Behavioural Styles

reading.source_scope_note: Three online observational-video surveys comparing pairs of Pepper interaction styles. Participants rate the robot and make forced relative capacity choices; they do not directly interact with a robot or perform a validated theory-of-mind task.
access_limits: All eleven pages, Figures 1–3, Tables 1–4, full bibliography and declarations read. Figure 2’s three screenshots show the same robot/task scene and differently colored eyes; the actual videos/audio, timing and complete scripts were not obtained.

No supplementary-material or data-availability link was found in the inspected publisher page or supplied PDF. No raw dataset, analysis script, registration or prior style-validation study was obtained; absence of a located link is not proof that no materials exist.

Targeted source identity checks verify Gray/Wegner, Russell/Mehrabian, Dennett and Spatola/Wykowska. Crossref itself inverts the last two authors’ name fields; DBLP corroborates their identities. The cited ScienceDirect source returned 403, and none of these studies/books is counted as fully read.
No author contact, external message, source-program execution or participant-data download occurred.

study.recruitment: 175 volunteers aged 18–67 recruited without payment through different social media channels. 29 fail a robot-name validation question; 146 remain: Authoritarian–Neutral 43 of 52, Friendly–Neutral 60 of 66, Friendly–Authoritarian 43 of 57. Different channels were intended to avoid overlap, but no cross-survey deduplication method is shown.
study.design: Each survey compares two videos of the same Pepper guiding a male actor through the same 15-second attentive-matrices exercise. Video order is randomized. Participants first rate each video with Godspeed plus added valence/arousal/dominance items and a 14-item trust scale; then choose which of the two styles better reflects each of 18 capacities. The three pairwise samples are not a single three-style repeated-measures sample.
study.style_bundle: Friendly/Neutral/Authoritarian jointly vary eye color, gaze, feedback, gesture, speech rate, pitch and formal/informal language. Friendly encourages, Neutral gives no feedback, Authoritarian makes attention/time commands. Effects cannot be uniquely assigned to warmth, eye color, a particular emotion or a single linguistic feature.
study.scoring: One binary style choice per item, with no neither/equal option. Eleven experience and seven agency choices are summed. The two compared styles’ scores necessarily sum to 11 or 7 for each person, so equal within-pair SDs are expected and relative scores do not measure absolute mental capacity or belief in sentience.
study.analysis: Per-item chi-square goodness-of-fit tests and within-person Wilcoxon comparisons of the two domain sums. Bonferroni is applied to 20 tests per survey; .05/20 is .0025, while the text prints p<.002. Spearman associations are analyzed at nominal .05 without a declared multiplicity correction.
study.authoritarian_neutral: Personality and consciousness favor Authoritarian at corrected significance. The experience sum 6.30 vs 4.70 gives Z=−2.968, p=.003 and does not pass either .002 or .0025. Agency is nonsignificant. Figure 3A’s significance claim contradicts the corrected Results text.
study.friendly_neutral: Friendly receives more hunger, pleasure, desire, personality, consciousness and joy choices; Neutral receives more fear/rage choices after correction. Friendly receives more emotion recognition, communication and thought choices. Both aggregate sums pass corrected thresholds, but not every capacity does.
study.friendly_authoritarian: Friendly wins hunger, pleasure, desire, consciousness and joy; Authoritarian wins fear, pain and rage after correction. Friendly wins morality, emotion recognition, communication and thought; both aggregate sums pass. Pride was part of the initial negative-emotion prediction but does not pass corrected significance.
study.correlations: Pooled within-style datasets contain Neutral 103, Authoritarian 86, Friendly 103 observations. Neutral agency–perceived safety ρ=.245, p=.013 and Authoritarian agency–likeability ρ=.213, p=.049 are nominal associations. No significant trust association is reported. Pairwise comparators and survey demographics differ, so pooling does not make these absolute style scores or prove a style-by-correlation interaction.
study.demographics: The Authoritarian–Neutral group’s mean age is 43.51, Friendly–Neutral 29.00, Friendly–Authoritarian 26.67. Within-pair comparisons retain randomized presentation order, while across-survey effect/rank comparisons and pooled correlations may mix comparator and sample differences.
study.not_measured: Actual robot emotion/consciousness/morality, human theory-of-mind task performance, objective robot safety, behavioral trust/reliance, clinical/cognitive improvement and the causal reason for a null trust correlation are not measured.

summary: The same robot’s bundled interaction styles change relative capacity choices. This enriches existing mind/experience/agency concepts without a new synonym entry; retain forced-choice measurement, corrected versus nominal significance, mixed item results and unresolved reporting limits.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich a documented construct with the pairwise behavioral-style design rather than count a scale, style label or existing facet as another behavior.

evidence.quote: as follows: participants were asked to choose which one

findings.evidence_scope: Three pairwise video surveys adapt the 18-capacity questionnaire to forced choices. Friendly tends to receive higher domain sums against both alternatives; Authoritarian–Neutral has selected item differences without a corrected domain-sum effect.
findings.boundary: Relative forced-choice scores depend on the comparison partner and cannot show absolute mental capacity, a universal two-factor mind structure, genuine machine consciousness or human ToM performance.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich a documented construct with the pairwise behavioral-style design rather than count a scale, style label or existing facet as another behavior.

evidence.quote: Neutral interaction style was more capable of experiencing

findings.evidence_scope: Experience ratings vary by specific capacity: Friendly is chosen for joy/pleasure/desire and others; Neutral or Authoritarian can be chosen for fear/rage, and Authoritarian for pain relative to Friendly. Domain sums retain both positive- and negative-valence items.
findings.boundary: Perceived emotion is not felt emotion. Consciousness and personality are capacity items rather than intrinsically positive emotions; the source’s broad positive-emotion label should not erase mixed item patterns or the null corrected Authoritarian–Neutral domain result.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich a documented construct with the pairwise behavioral-style design rather than count a scale, style label or existing facet as another behavior.

evidence.quote: scored significantly higher on ToM’s Experience and Agency

findings.evidence_scope: Friendly receives more emotion-recognition, communication and thought choices than Neutral, and more morality plus those capacities than Authoritarian. Aggregate agency differences pass correction in these two comparisons.
findings.boundary: The seven-item relative score is not verified thought, moral agency or operational competence. No corrected Authoritarian–Neutral domain difference is established; the pairwise results are not a tested universal ordering of all three styles.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich a documented construct with the pairwise behavioral-style design rather than count a scale, style label or existing facet as another behavior.

findings.evidence_scope: The introduction uses ToM as a theoretical explanation of mental-state inference and contrasts cognitive and affective facets. The experiment measures capacity attribution to a robot rather than accuracy in inferring false beliefs or human emotions.
findings.boundary: Do not equate an attributed ability with the observer’s validated mentalizing skill or robot ToM performance. No independent full cited-source study or book was read.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s emotional state from their situation and behavior, without necessarily sharing that emotion.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich a documented construct with the pairwise behavioral-style design rather than count a scale, style label or existing facet as another behavior.

findings.evidence_scope: Background-only definition distinguishes recognizing another’s emotional state from understanding beliefs. It helps keep felt experience attribution separate from mental-state inference.
findings.boundary: This paper does not administer a human affective-ToM performance test or demonstrate emotional sharing, and its experience subscore is not an interchangeable measure of that skill.

findings.definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich a documented construct with the pairwise behavioral-style design rather than count a scale, style label or existing facet as another behavior.

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary-only result: the broad 14-item robot-trust measure shows no reported significant association with capacity-choice sums in the three style datasets. The paper speculates that indirect noncooperative viewing may explain this.
findings.boundary: This broad trust instrument is not an isolated performance-trust measure. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence or a causal explanation; the proposed direct/cooperative follow-up has not been tested.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The seven Authoritarian item counts sum to 162, implying mean 162/43=3.7674, whereas the printed aggregate is 3.74. Neutral counts imply 139/43=3.2326, agreeing with 3.23. Reported means sum to 6.97 rather than the required seven. Which count/mean is wrong cannot be determined without data; do not silently change the original aggregate.

The plot positions experience and agency sums with different maximum totals (11 versus seven), each relative to a different opponent. It is not an absolute common-capacity scale or a single three-style ranking; raw axis positions and equal SDs must not be interpreted as independent measurements.

Two domain scores × nine Godspeed/VAD/trust scales × three styles allow many nominal comparisons, while only p=.013 and .049 associations are highlighted. No multiplicity correction, comparator-adjusted model or direct difference-of-correlations test is reported. Do not infer that relationships differ significantly across styles.

Several predicted items, notably pride, do not survive correction, and trust correlations are not significant. Narrow the claim to supported item/subscore comparisons and nominal Godspeed associations; no blanket confirmation of every prediction or causal null explanation follows.

Several references contain further suspicious given-name/surname or abbreviated locator fields. Only the selected identities above were verified; no wholesale automatic repair or invented DOI is applied.

methodological_limits: Three small convenience samples recruited through separate social media channels; 29 of 175 excluded by an end-of-video name check. Hearing/recalling a colored robot name is not a complete attention, exposure or unbiased selection guarantee.

The intended cross-survey separation is not a verified deduplication protocol. Within-pair order is randomized, while assignment across surveys is not described as randomized and mean ages differ substantially.
The style manipulation bundles verbal and nonverbal cues and a single actor/task setting. It does not identify whether eye color, voice, feedback or role expectation causes an item-specific effect.

Capacity choices are forced relative judgments with complementary sums, not independent absolute capacities. Neither no-mind nor equal-attribution options are available; score increases for one member mechanically reduce the other.

Per-item chi-square tests compare each person’s choice with equal-frequency expectation; repeated items are not new independent participants. Wilcoxon uses the within-person summed comparison. The main paired analyses are not mislabeled as wholly independent rows.

Reliability alpha alone does not validate the new VAD additions’ three-factor structure, measurement invariance or accurate emotion recognition. Actual videos, scripts and original instrument interface were not independently inspected.

Corrected primary item/domain tests differ from the nominal exploratory correlation family. Nonsignificance is not equivalence, and a significant correlation in one style but not another is not a formal moderator test.

ToM task accuracy, actual robot mentality/morality, real safety, behavioral trust, clinical benefit and cooperation outcomes were not measured. Observation of a video is not direct HRI, a limitation the authors acknowledge.
The pandemic/indirect-task explanation for null trust associations is speculative, not an identified cause. Recommendations to improve acceptance are proposals, not proven intervention benefits.

No participant data, code, preregistration or prior style-validation study was obtained. Own count/threshold calculations verify printed arithmetic only and do not reproduce original participant-level analyses.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Forced or constrained lexical choices need explicit interpretation. Here complementary binary selections do not establish absolute dimensions or universal capacity structure.
Human mind attribution can show multiple facet structures. These inherited 11/7 item sums are operational scales rather than evidence against other supported dimensional accounts.
Trust, sharing intentions and capacity attribution are distinct. Null or pooled associations cannot be relabeled causal trust improvements.

Role and style information can change perceived capacity, but actual feelings, rights and a universal two-dimensional architecture remain unverified. Preserve appropriate paired analyses and correct only the separately problematic inference/reporting.

deferred.term: Friendly, Neutral and Authoritarian as three new behaviors
deferred.reason: These are composite experimental style conditions, not three newly isolated psychological mechanisms; existing communication and mind-attribution concepts cover relevant parts.

deferred.term: Cognitive theory of mind as another row from this source
deferred.reason: Background overlaps the existing Theory of mind / mentalizing definition; no separate performance task or distinct validated mechanism is introduced.
Respondents make relative choices for mixed capacity items; neither actual sentience nor two new types of robot feeling is demonstrated.
The reported trust associations are nonsignificant and no behavioral reliance benefit is established.

limitations: No new row; reliable evidence and inference boundaries enrich existing concepts. Eleven categories, stable IDs and unnumbered rows preserved. No invented timelines, automatic ethical/harm edges, full-book reading credit or full-paper Markdown copy.
